_meta.rule: Only values read on a NASA page, each with the page id (see sources.json). No game-balance numbers and no our-own-formula numbers live here. All pages were read on 2026-11-06 through a summarizing tool, so check each against its page (see the Verify sheet in the spreadsheet).

pressure_min.label: Surface pressure, low end of seasonal range
pressure_min.page_says: Varies from 4.0 to 8.7 mb with season

pressure_max.label: Surface pressure, high end of seasonal range
pressure_max.page_says: Varies from 4.0 to 8.7 mb with season

temp_min.label: Minimum surface temperature
temp_min.page_says: 184 K (-89 C) at the Viking 1 lander site

temp_max.label: Maximum surface temperature
temp_max.page_says: 242 K (-31 C) at the Viking 1 lander site

sol_hours.label: Length of a Martian solar day

co2_pct.label: Carbon dioxide in the surface atmosphere

rad_gale_surface.label: Radiation on the Mars surface at Gale (dose equivalent, average Aug 2012 to Jun 2013)
rad_gale_surface.page_says: An average of 0.67 millisieverts per day from August 2012 to June 2013

rad_gale_absorbed_gcr.label: Galactic cosmic ray absorbed dose rate at the surface
rad_gale_absorbed_gcr.page_says: A slowly varying dose rate of about 210 micrograys per day

rad_cruise.label: Radiation on the trip to Mars (galactic cosmic rays)
rad_cruise.page_says: Average of 1.8 milliSieverts of GCR per day on its journey to Mars

tau_3_sunlight.label: Share of sunlight that reaches the ground at tau 3
tau_3_sunlight.page_says: A tau of three indicates that only about 5 percent of the sunlight entering the atmosphere directly reaches the surface

tau_opportunity_2018.label: Tau at Opportunity, 10 June 2018
tau_opportunity_2018.page_says: Estimated tau of 10.8 as of Sunday morning (10 June)

storm_first_detected.label: 2018 storm first detected
storm_first_detected.page_says: First detected the storm on Wednesday, May 30

storm_decay_began.label: 2018 storm began to decay
storm_decay_began.page_says: July 23: dust was settling faster than it was being lifted

storm_shape.label: Shape of the 2018 storm
storm_shape.value: growth over about a month, near the peak for three weeks, then a multi-month decay
storm_shape.page_says: Complex growth over the first month, near the peak for three weeks, then a multi-month decay

gale_elevation.label: Gale Crater landing-site elevation
gale_elevation.page_says: Minus 4,501 meters elevation (page names no datum)

gale_air_temp_high.label: Gale Crater daily air temperature high (REMS)
gale_air_temp_high.page_says: Daily highs at about 32 F (0 C)

gale_air_temp_low.label: Gale Crater daily air temperature low (REMS)
gale_air_temp_low.page_says: Lows at about minus 94 F (minus 70 C)

meridiani_lat.label: Meridiani Planum (Opportunity landing site) latitude
meridiani_lat.note: Printed as "-1.95°N" on the page; read here as 1.95 S. Confirm on another NASA page.

deuteronilus_lat.label: Deuteronilus Mensae point latitude
deuteronilus_lat.page_says: Image centered at 42.2 degrees north latitude
deuteronilus_lat.note: Centre of one NASA image, used as the site point.

arcadia_lat.label: Arcadia Planitia point latitude
arcadia_lat.note: Location of one NASA image, used as the site point.

arcadia_ice_depth.label: Depth of ice in parts of Arcadia Planitia (upper bound)
arcadia_ice_depth.page_says: Less than one foot (30 centimeters) below the surface

ice_best_regions.label: Regions with the most remote-sensing evidence for accessible ice (northern mid-latitudes)
ice_best_regions.page_says: The broad plains of Arcadia and the extensive glacial networks across Deuteronilus Mensae match the greatest number of remote-sensing criteria

crew_oxygen.label: Oxygen per crewmember per day (82 kg reference astronaut, 90 min exercise)
crew_oxygen.page_says: A daily O2 requirement of 0.89 kg

crew_oxygen_rest.label: Oxygen per crewmember per day, at rest

crew_oxygen_exercise.label: Oxygen per crewmember per day, with exercise

crew_water.label: Minimum drinking water per crewmember per day
crew_water.page_says: Minimum 2.5 L per crewmember per day
crew_water.note: Hygiene water is mission dependent; NASA gives no number.

crew_kcal.label: Average energy per crewmember per day

crew_food_packaged.label: As-packaged food mass per crewmember per day (ISS planning value)
crew_food_packaged.page_says: BVAD Table 4-53 ISS planning value 2.39 kg
